incident-bot: Pager ALERT (P1) — Customer 'Lumina Health' Direct Connect (dx-237) path oscillation in eu-west-2. Route flaps detected, elevated error rate to hosted endpoints. Paging oncall. :rotating_light:

Nina C: ack — I'm on call, looking. Can someone grab a quick customer impact summary?

Mike L: saw spikes in 502s for a subset of requests (API write path). Cloud metrics show TCP retransmits and BGP neighbor resets on the partner side.

Nina C: pulling BGP adjacency now.

Nina C: ```
# bgp summary on router-rdx-euw2
Neighbor        AS      MsgRcvd MsgSent  TblVer  InQ OutQ Up/Down  State/PfxRcd
10.10.11.5      64512   125342  125330  16777216 0   0   00:12:34  204
10.10.12.6      64513   125210  125295  16777216 0   0   00:00:15  Idle
```

Nina C: neighbor to partner ASN 64513 is flapping, second hop idle intermittently. Traceroute from a failing request shows path switching between dx-237 and dx-242.

Henry K: @Nina C good catch. Sounds like partial multipath instability — provider-level BGP churn. Is there an active failover to dx-242?

Nina C: Yes, dx-242 exists as standby, but some routes are pinned at the app layer (session affinity). That explains why only a portion of traffic errors.

Sara D: Customer impact: Lumina reported 12% error increase for write calls 01:08–01:35 UTC, some user-facing retries. No bulk data loss. I've DMed account manager and scheduled a postmortem call.

ops-sre-bot: Automated mitigation candidate: prep withdraw of low-priority /24 more-specifics, apply local-preference to prefer dx-242, and request partner to enable dampening on problematic prefixes.

Nina C: I'm going to try a conservative local-pref shift on our eBGP session to prefer dx-242 for the affected prefixes. Will announce before change.

Henry K: +1. Keep changes scoped — prefer route, don't withdraw. If flaps continue we can withdraw the more-specifics temporarily.

Nina C: making change now — running config diff:
```
router bgp 65000
 neighbor 10.10.12.6 route-map PREF-DX242 in
!
route-map PREF-DX242 permit 10
 set local-preference 200
```

Nina C: applied. BGP table now shows preferred path via 10.10.12.6 (dx-242) for affected prefixes.

Mike L: seeing drop in error rate already — 502s down from 12% -> 3% in the last 3 minutes. Good sign.

incident-bot: Note: change logged by ops runbook (CR# 2026-0009).

Nina C: I'll open a case with partner NOC and request they look at their uplink to our ASN 64513. Sharing our adjacency logs and timestamps.

Nina C: ```
# tail -n 50 /var/log/bgp/adj.log
2026-03-15T01:02:14Z BGP Rcv UPDATE from 10.10.11.5, withdrawn 0, attrs 12
2026-03-15T01:08:03Z BGP session reset to 10.10.12.6, reason: hold-timer expired
2026-03-15T01:08:04Z BGP session reestablished to 10.10.12.6
```

Henry K: Partner responded via ticket — they see a flapping interface on their aggregation switch. They've put the port into a monitored state and will replace optics if it recurs. They asked if we can keep pref to dx-242 for 2 hours.

Nina C: Agreed. I'll keep the route-map for 2 hours and set a reminder to revert.

Mike L: service pain window narrowed. Suggest we schedule a brief handoff to next oncall in 30m and mark incident as "mitigated, monitoring".

Sara D: Customer update sent: "We mitigated routing instability by temporarily shifting traffic to an alternate path. We're monitoring and working with our network partner. No data lost; some retries experienced. Will follow up soon."

Nina C: Handoff plan — @Mike L you take 03:10 UTC watch if no new flaps. I'll leave the route-map in place until partner confirms optic swap. If we see re-flap, escalate to P0 and we'll withdraw more-specifics.

Mike L: ack. Taking handoff at 03:10 UTC. Will keep monitoring BGP peers and error rates.

ops-sre-bot: Handoff logged: from Nina C -> Mike L at 03:10 UTC. Incident state: MITIGATED (observed reduced error rate). Ticket: INC-2143657890.

Nina C: quick follow-ups for postmortem:
- Confirm partner root cause (they suspect intermittent optic degradation)
- Confirm why session did not failover cleanly for all traffic (session affinity/pinning investigation)
- Consider automated local-pref playbook to activate for similar future flaps

Henry K: I'll add a checklist item to the runbook to verify app-level affinity settings when we have multi-dx setups.

Sara D: closing customer-facing note after partner confirms swap. Will open postmortem doc and invite network, infra, and solutions engineering.

Mike L: monitoring looks good for now. Leaving this thread pinned under the incident channel. If anything changes I'll reopen and page. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident resolved -> MITIGATED. Monitoring continues for 2 hours.
